extracted.intended_audience: researchers and academics who perform peer review of journal manuscripts (including early-career reviewers)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical, ten-point guidance for researchers acting as peer reviewers of scholarly manuscripts, covering timeliness, scope, methodology, reproducibility, presentation, ethics, and tone. Intended to help reviewers produce useful reports for editors and constructive feedback for authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respond promptly to review requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Respond promptly to review requests, accept or decline; recommend early-career researchers as alternatives when declining.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tell editors quickly whether you will review so they can secure alternatives; if you decline, suggest suitable reviewers (including early-career researchers) to help the editor find replacements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider dual audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments should help editors decide and give authors constructive feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write reports that serve two purposes: provide a clear recommendation and evidence for the editor, and give authors actionable, constructive suggestions to improve the manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize methodology and data assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Prioritize methodology and data assessment; once those are sound, interpretation issues are usually easier to fix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus first on study design, data quality, analysis and methods; methodological flaws or data problems are more critical than stylistic or interpretive issues and may undermine conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review the submitted manuscript, not the paper you would have written
rubrics_metrics.description: Review the manuscript that was submitted, not the paper you would have written.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge the work on its own terms and within its stated scope; avoid imposing your preferred framing or demanding that authors completely rewrite their study into your ideal version.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Verify reproducibility — sufficient information for others to replicate the study and interpret findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that methods, data, and (where applicable) code are described or available at a level that would allow others to reproduce the analyses or understand how results were obtained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate presentation quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate presentation quality — clarity, abstract accuracy, whether figures fairly represent results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess clarity of writing, whether the abstract accurately reflects the paper, and whether figures/tables honestly and clearly present the data (labels, legends, scales, and representations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggest readability improvements without formally editing
rubrics_metrics.description: Suggest improvements to readability without formally editing; flag language quality issues that obscure scientific content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point out where phrasing, structure or organization could be improved and give examples or suggestions, but do not perform line-by-line copy-editing; flag serious language issues that impede understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flag integrity concerns to editors
rubrics_metrics.description: Flag integrity concerns including ethics, data availability, and transparency to editors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Raise potential ethical problems, concerns about data access or transparency, or other integrity issues privately to the editor rather than airing them in public-facing comments to authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge competency limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge competency limits — tell the editor what you cannot properly assess.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be transparent about areas outside your expertise (e.g., specific statistical techniques, specialized methods) so editors can weigh your judgments appropriately or seek additional reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review your own report carefully before sending
rubrics_metrics.description: Review your own report carefully before sending — clarity, professionalism, politeness, no accidental personal details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proofread your review for tone and clarity; ensure comments are professional and constructive, avoid personal or identifying details you did not intend to share, and remove any accidental insults or unprofessional language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guiding principle: reciprocity in reviewing
rubrics_metrics.description: "Review others as you want to be reviewed yourself."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt the golden-rule approach: be constructive, fair and respectful in critiques, remembering that authors are colleagues who will likely be reviewers in return.
